items.text: PHP2Shell, day five: the public exploit technique has now been seen working end to end in the wild. An independent honeypot report dated Oct 24 correlates 35 shell starts with 35 exploit requests on three single-worker PHP 8.4.26 decoys, from two hosting addresses, Friday 15:35 to 18:57 UTC. Deliberately easy targets, no victims; still no organization confirmed breached by name, still no CISA listing (checked 13:15 ET), still no PHP release since Oct 21.

Japan's emergency alerts are coming back after the precautionary PHP shutdown: NTT Docomo restored Area Mail (J-Alert, flood and evacuation warnings) in full at 20:01 JST Sunday, a night earlier than planned; SoftBank has earthquake and tsunami warnings back since 09:25 JST, with government evacuation alerts due Oct 26. Nepal's thousands of government sites await a central patch from Sunday evening.

New to the index: Israel votes Tuesday after a campaign in which a sitting finance minister posted an AI video of the Supreme Court president and attorney general being dragged from a protest, the prime minister shared one evoking a rival's son killed in Gaza, and bots built against Iran were turned to Likud, per Al Jazeera and Haaretz. A university monitor is reported to have found about one in eight election posts AI-made.

Also new: Nigeria's cybercrime police say a 23-year-old used AI voice cloning and deepfakes to pose as Elon Musk in a crypto scheme, one of nine arrests made with the UK's NCA, the RCMP and Germany's BKA; $15,900 in crypto recovered. And Spain's PP deepfake ad now faces a criminal complaint before the Audiencia Nacional for defamation and digital identity theft.
